answer: Each new identity must post a verifiable delay function proof of 2^26 sequential squarings, which takes about 20 minutes on one core and cannot be parallelized. Difficulty doubles for every extra identity sharing a funding ancestor within 90 days, so the tenth fake costs 512 times the first in wall-clock time. Validators verify each proof in milliseconds and reject reef-linked clusters that repeat the same seed. A whisper of shared timing or a quartz-clear common funder triggers the doubling automatically.
